heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings and their chaining values cv = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: within one chaining value the 2^26 table values F(a0) behave as independent uniform words (expected occupancy occ = 1 - (1 - 2^-26)^(2^26) = 0.632121, uniform tags, 160 occ 2^26 / 2^32 = 1.58030 claws per scan word); F7 has probability |F7|/2^32; the X_j and the online works W_j of different chaining values are independent (proof.md Lemma 3, Section 7).
heuristics.scope: The expected claw count, the mean online work wbar (hence V_MAX), the independence used by Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3) and the product over chaining values in the success bound (proof.md Sections 5, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our flat-table C port (dev/claw/t6.c) at 2^26 slots loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 measured occupancy 0.632152 to 0.632218 on four chaining values (formula 0.632121) and 1.57372 to 1.57452 claws per scanned word over 2^23 scan words each, against the formula 160 occ / 2^6 = 1.58046 (ratio 0.9957 to 0.9963); the parent's packed port measured 0.63216 and 0.99898. The organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws, reference claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values. The scan words u0 + n are distinct and u0 is a fresh random word per chaining value, so the scan adds no dependence (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem: within each chaining value the table values F(a0), their tags and the claws found are taken to follow the per-chaining-value random-function law; independent first blocks do not by themselves prove it. Checked at reduced and full table size on a few chaining values, not on 2^53.9 of them.

heuristics.statement: For the claws the procedure finds, Pr[C1 and C2 and G and F7] = q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the rate enumerated exhaustively over all 2^32 words (P(C1) = 1/8, |C1 and C2| = 53,096,854, the window-R = 9 G count 57,726,359,870,197, |F7| = 287,309,824); the stage rates 1/8, 2^-6.3379, 2^-12.2857 set the mean post-filter cost.
heuristics.scope: The good pairs per chaining value (62,193.16) and the mean post-filter work in wbar (proof.md Sections 5, 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: Section 7 already takes E[K] over all 2^32 scan words, and this filing's ledger scans all 2^32 words u = u0 + n per chaining value, so the ledger and the probability analysis use the same scan. Our C port at n0 = 2^26 measured occupancy 0.63216 and claws/expected 0.99898 over 2^20 scan words; the organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values, and the scan words u0 + n are distinct with u0 a fresh random word per chaining value (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise that the exhaustive rates hold for the claws found; F7 is chaining-value dependent (measured heterogeneity 1.254).

heuristics.statement: A good pair is accepted by step 3b with probability q3r >= q3_P1 x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.4010, where q3_P1 = 2^-96.0791 = q3_model x 2^D_LB: q3_model = 2^-96.0133 is the registered accepted-event rate of the A0-variant good pairs on P8 before row 16 (row 16 has probability 160/2^32 and a P1 good pair has passed it) and D_LB = -0.0658 is the registered one-sided 99% lower bound of the paired per-seed difference L(P1) - L(A0) measured with the P1 law of this package's window (a0 in [9 x 2^26, 10 x 2^26) given G, a1 uniform on C1 and C2). This filing inherits the bound unchanged: the table retune does not touch q3, q3r, the relaxation ratio, the paired R9 run or any part of the transfer, and the identical bound (q3_model 2^-96.0133, D_LB -0.0658, ratio +0.41488) is the one this workspace's accepted row 711c4bf8 and its predecessor a32131ff were scored on.
heuristics.extrapolation: Registered runs, per-seed values and registration hashes in proof.md (Section 9, Appendices P, Q, R.1): level -96.42816 (128 seeds), ratio +0.41488 (400 seeds), paired P1 difference R9 D = -0.0121, sd 0.1321, n = 36, D_LB = -0.0658 (declared), and the earlier A25 run on the window [0, 2^25) D = +0.0022, D_LB = -0.0345 (n = 76, reported). Every diagnostic 0.
heuristics.limitations: Three Monte-Carlo bounds (level, relaxation ratio, paired P1 difference), each by a rule registered before its run; joint confidence at least 97%% (union bound). The relaxation ratio (row-18 relation E18 = E17 not imposed) is measured on the A0 family and applied to the P1 family. The paired runs use the printed-cell event; their P1 pairs are drawn from the exact law of C1, C2, G on the window, not from claws of the procedure (F7 is the separate late word W7, as in the A0 runs). The complete event (about 2^-71 per good pair) is not observed by any organizer run. The relaxation ratio is measured on the A0 family and applied to the P1 family; the argument is that the relaxed cells (E17, E18) are read identically by both families and that the paired R9 run measures the family difference on the printed-cell event. This is the parent's premise, unchanged and unweakened here.

heuristics.statement: Group independence within a chaining value (the form of H5-group-independence of the accepted 44870635): good pairs of one chaining value that share no endpoint (a0 or u) are independent trials of the accepted event, each with probability q3r; good pairs sharing an endpoint form a group counted once. Consequence used: for a uniform chaining value, J (accepted good pairs over all 2^32 scan words) has E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J].
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor (1 - 2^-8.5) per chaining value. Lemma 4 (proof.md Section 7) derives E[X_j(X_j-1)]/E[X_j] <= E[J(J-1)]/E[J] exactly from the distinct scan words u0 + n with u0 uniform.
heuristics.extrapolation: Under the statement E[J(J-1)]/E[J] = q3r E[K(K-1)]/E[K] <= q3r E[K] x 1.246 = 2^-54.61, below 2^-7.5 by a factor 2^47.1 (K = good pairs per chaining value, E[K] = 2^16.47; 1.246 = the measured E[K^2]/E[K]^2 over 24 chaining values, proof.md Appendix H). Panel: 0 of 2,124 good pairs share an endpoint; C2|C1 and G|C1C2 binomial across chaining values; F7 overdispersed (it reads the chaining value). Registered test on components of the accepted event (proof.md Appendix H.2): Part B of the 10-17 registration, run unchanged on 10-21: the forced-bit events B_t = ((E_t^x & m_t) == v_t) of rows 17..21 (the value-only cells of E17..E21, rates 2^-7, 2^-7, 2^-3, 2^-5, 2^-4), computed on the real compressions of both members of every good pair, ONE = every good pair of one chaining value over all 2^32 scan words (17,576; the registered target 20,000 exceeds what the chaining value has), MANY = 100 good pairs of each of 200 chaining values (20,000), all re-verified by an independent rebuild (0 and 0 bad): against N p_t the largest |z| is 2.43 (ONE) and 1.58 (MANY); ONE against MANY on rates, |z| at most 1.57; dispersion of E19, E20, E21 across the 200 chaining values chi-square 205.2, 190.2, 193.3 on 199 dof (two-sided p 0.734, 0.680, 0.798). The registered ONE-against-MANY formula (n1 - n2)/sqrt(n1 + n2) assumes equal sizes; applied to the unequal sizes it gives |z| up to 3.77, which is the size difference, not dependence (Appendix H.2). No within-chaining-value dependence of these components is detected.
heuristics.limitations: Independence of the rows 17..37 event between good pairs of one chaining value is not testable at any sample size and is the premise. The registered Part B test covers the forced-bit components of rows 17..21 only, not the full rows 17..37 event; C1 clusters in scan order (u's high bits) and F7 varies with the chaining value; both are measured and enter the derivation as the spread factor.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: The search for P8 was run by the author of 1a695f0b, whose published run log (38 solver runs, 230,183 s listed) and total (under 2^21 core-seconds) are quoted with their source hash in proof.md Appendix R.4: at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second that is 2^43.61 units, 34.4 bits under A_C. Our own measurements of the same kind of computation (proof.md Appendix R.2): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; a 38-step pair from the published cells in 2^34.09 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full): we did not rerun P8's search; its log is the author's, quoted. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 84.96832.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) is obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74).
heuristics.extrapolation: The Step-1 solve was run by the author of 1a695f0b (coupling check 662 s, single-threaded, inside the quoted total under 2^21 core-seconds; proof.md Appendix R.4); our own 38-step pair search from the published cells took 2,852.83 CPU-seconds = 2^34.09 units (proof.md Appendix R.2), 39.9 bits under A_S. selftest checks that the transcribed pair S reproduces and passes every test of rows 16..21 with equal outputs.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement; its support is the author-reported core-seconds. The Step-1 peak memory, re-measured under a 2^28 cap at 2^27.7542 (377cb363), is below the online cell 2^28.01141, which is the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development computation of this package, whether or not the procedure reads its output (exhaustive passes, C ports, the q3 and ratio studies, the F7 measurement, checks, failed runs and reruns), is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions, and DEV is charged in full in the time.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70 x C operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware envelope (the bound for this allowance): every code execution of the project (10-05 to 10-21) ran on a 24-thread workstation with one GPU, a 12-thread server and one 32-vCPU cloud machine: at most 68 threads and one GPU for 1.4688 x 10^6 s at 2^40 word operations per thread-second and 2^47 per GPU-second, below 2^68.11 operations = 2^56.7 compressions, under DEV by more than 2^13; the recorded development of the A0-variant line is in proof.md Appendix R.3.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: the hardware envelope above is the bound; it rests on the project's machine list and dates, and is more than 2^13 below the charge.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 (256-bit word RAM) the claw table is a flat array of 2^26 32-bit slots (2^28 bytes, the same allocation as the parent's packed layout): a slot access is index shift 1, address add 1, load 1 = 3 operations and a slot store is address add 1 + store 1 = 2 on top of the entry computation, with no lane extraction. The per-chaining-value reset to SENT covers all 2^26 slots with 2^23 256-bit stores of 5 operations (store 1, address add 1, loop 3). The parent's packed layout is priced in the same table as the alternative (7 and 11 per access and store, appendix A.14 and R.7), and every other operation of the procedure -- work-counter adds (1), the empty-slot test (2), the post-filters, and step 3b at 3,014 -- is unchanged and counted at the unit costs of fb176310 (S0/S1/s0/s1 8, CH 3, MAJ 4, compare-and-branch 2, the rest 1).
heuristics.scope: The counted operations of the online procedure (proof.md Sections 4, 5, Appendix A.14): 303.670 per claw (scan, post-filters, reset and build, the table build amortised over 2^32 scan words) and 3,014 per step 3b.
heuristics.extrapolation: run_claw counts every operation; selftest checks the counted run against the per-u charge of Section 5; our flat port's measured claw rate 1.5737-1.5745 per word agrees with 160 occ / 2^6 to 0.4%; the parent's own registered design table (P1_TEST.md, quoted in proof.md R.7) prices the flat and packed layouts separately (flat 2.035, packed 1.594 at n0 = 2^26).
heuristics.limitations: The ledger is an exact analytic count read from the code, not a measurement; it does not rely on the organizer runs' counted_ops (reduced size). The unit costs are the fb176310 convention; the packed access sequence is the explicit list of proof.md Section 4.

heuristics.statement: The counted memory cell is the claimed peak over the counted phases: the parent's measured 264,224 KiB = 270,565,376 bytes = 2^28.01141 of the full-table C-port execution of the online program (2^26 slots of 32 bits = 2^28 bytes, plus advice, registers, scan state and code), unchanged by this revision because the flat table is the same 2^28 bytes; our own flat port measures 263,836 KiB = 2^28.0093, below it. It is above every other counted cell: the Step-1 solve at 2^27.7542 (377cb363) and the author's signed search at 2^27.92 (Appendix R.4).
heuristics.scope: The memory metric and the score 83.44485 + (28.01141 - 20) = 91.45626.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our flat-table port (dev/claw/t6.c) ran with a peak resident set of 263,836 KiB = 270,168,064 bytes = 2^28.0093 (ru_maxrss, four chaining values, build and scan); the parent's packed port of the same 2^28-byte table measured 264,224 KiB. Every development execution ran under address-space caps of at most 2^28 bytes (proof.md Appendix R.3).
heuristics.limitations: The cell is the parent's measured online peak, unchanged; the flat access changes no table bytes and therefore no memory. The post-filters and step 3b allocate no table and are not part of that measurement, and both preprocessing cells (2^27.7542 and 2^27.92) are below it.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; step 3b accepts a pair only if A34..A37, E34..E37 of both members are equal, so every output is a collision (Lemma 1, proof.md Section 1).

Algorithm (proof.md Sections 2, 3, Appendix A.14; experiments/p1claw38.py): per chaining value a 2^26-slot table over a0 in window R = 9, held as a FLAT array of 32-bit words (one slot per word, 2^28 bytes; the entry is the 26-bit a0 offset and the low 6 bits of F(a0)), and a scan of the 2^32 distinct words u = u0 + n; a claw (a0, u) has E16x = F(a0) + s0(u) - u in the 160-word row-16 set; claws pass the post-filters C1, C2, G, F7 on the real words; every good pair runs step 3b (Step 2, rows 16..37 of both members, the P8 tests of rows 16..21 with early abort, output comparison).

Cost: the procedure scans 2^32 distinct words u = u0 + n (mod 2^32) per chaining value, the same scan Section 7 of the proof counts good pairs over; N_CV = 16,994,757,457,699,444 chaining values (each one first block: one compression plus 75 operations, inside the per-chaining-value work); online work counted per operation (slot access index+address+load = 3, slot store 2, no lane extraction, work-counter adds, step 3b 3,014) with mean wbar = 2.061387e12 per chaining value (the 2^26-candidate table build at 38 per candidate and the 2^23 x 5 table reset included), capped at V_MAX = ceil((1 + 2^-16) N_CV wbar) = 35,033,298,321,167,006,489,444,653,178, cap tested per chaining value, OVER = vmax = 1,072,597,659,814,643. N = (2^78 + 2^74 + 2^70) C + V_MAX + OVER + FIN = 35,912,536,847,147,646,850,861,689,245 = 2^83.44485 compressions (C = 2,728).

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values), H1-P1 (q_pf = 2^-16.1877 for claws), H2-P1 (q3r >= 2^-71.4010 per good pair: the registered q3_model 2^-96.0133 plus the registered paired P1-vs-A0 lower bound -0.0658, measured on window R = 9, the only window this filing loads) and H3-P1 (group independence within a chaining value, giving E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]); Lemma 4 reduces the within-chaining-value term to H3-P1 exactly; Bonferroni per chaining value, independence across them, and Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3).

Memory: peak 2^28.01141 bytes = 264,224 KiB = 270,565,376 bytes, the parent's measured full-table C-port execution of the online program, UNCHANGED by this revision (the flat table is the same 2^26 slots in the same 2^28 bytes; our own flat port measures 2^28.0093 = 270,168,064 bytes, below it). It is the maximum over the counted phases: the Step-1 solve at 2^27.7542 (377cb363's capped re-measurement) and the author's signed search at 2^27.92 are both lower. H6. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 83.44485 + 8.01141 = 91.45626. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
